tools.name: bash
tools.description: Run one shell command in the workspace and return its output. Use read, write, edit, and grep for file work; bash is for builds, tests, package managers, git, and pipelines. Every call is a fresh shell, so cd and export do not carry over: pass cwd or chain commands with &&. Commands must finish on their own, because stdin is closed and a prompt cannot be answered. A non-zero exit is reported as an error, with the output still returned. stdout and stderr are returned as separate sections when both wrote, each keeping its start and its end; when a stream was truncated, its complete bytes are in the file named by stdout_full or stderr_full, so read or grep that file instead of re-running the command.

command.description: Shell command line, executed with the configured shell.

cwd.description: Directory to run in, relative to the workspace root or absolute. Defaults to the workspace root.

timeout_ms.description: Wall-clock budget for this call in milliseconds; clamped to the configured range.
